registry: single-source-of-truth authority map of the Scientific AI Harness
rule: each concept has exactly one executable authority; every other file is a consumer; documentation mirrors code and never overrides it
label: one executable authority per concept; documentation mirrors code and never overrides it

event_history.authority: agent_substrate/events.py :: EventLog -- the append-only, hash-chained log with a separately witnessed head; the only writable record of any decision
event_history.means: what happened, in order, tamper-evident: every other state below is a projection of it
event_history.does_not_mean: that an event is authorized: presence in the log is not authority, and every reader re-authorizes on replay

authority_fsm.authority: agent_substrate/authority.py :: the transition table and invariants I1-I6; agent_substrate/store.py :: AuthorityStore, the projection that re-authorizes every transition on replay
authority_fsm.means: which claims are PROPOSED, VERIFIED, PROMOTED or withdrawn, and who moved them
authority_fsm.does_not_mean: that a claim is true: PROMOTED means proposed, independently verified and promoted under a recorded policy

scientific_admission.authority: agent_substrate/result_rules.py :: admission policy scientific_result.admission/1, decided by the store live, on replay and on snapshot restore; restated independently in agent_substrate/reconstruct.py
scientific_admission.means: that a scientific_result's evidence -- a PASS from an independent implementation about this exact bundle, captured by governed tasks -- supports VERIFIED or PROMOTED
scientific_admission.does_not_mean: experimental validation: numerical verification admits a simulation result and nothing more

task_fsm.authority: agent_substrate/tasks.py :: the task transition table; agent_substrate/governed_tasks.py :: the projection on the production path; agent_substrate/reconstruct.py :: reconstruct_tasks, the second reader
task_fsm.means: whether a governed tool run was executed under lease and verified by an actor other than its executor
task_fsm.does_not_mean: that the tool's output is scientifically correct: a VERIFIED task is provenance

scheduler_fsm.authority: agent_substrate/scheduler.py :: the durable job queue -- readiness, leases, retry, cancellation
scheduler_fsm.means: which work is ready, running, finished or failed, across process deaths

memory_fsm.authority: agent_substrate/memory.py :: remembered facts and their status
memory_fsm.means: what an agent was told and still holds
memory_fsm.does_not_mean: evidence: memory is never cited as evidence

evidence_store.authority: agent_substrate/evidence.py :: EvidenceStore, content-addressed and append-only; every read re-hashes
evidence_store.means: the exact bytes a cited digest names (artifact integrity)
evidence_store.does_not_mean: scientific verification, or authority: the same bytes can be wrong

model_registry.means: which models exist, at which version, with which declared inputs
model_registry.does_not_mean: that a registered model is validated

scientific_result_schema.authority: scientific/result.py :: ResultBundle (to_record is the exact field set result_rules and reconstruct restate)
scientific_result_schema.means: what a model run produced, with its invariants, provenance and run identity
scientific_result_schema.does_not_mean: a measurement: a ResultBundle is a SIMULATION_RESULT

verification_schema.means: what a bounded check established, and how independent it was
verification_schema.does_not_mean: experimental validation, unless a COMPARISON_WITH_MEASUREMENT against measured observations says so

observation_schema.authority: scientific/observation.py :: Observation, ObservationKind and the lineage rules between kinds
observation_schema.means: what kind of thing a value is -- raw, processed, synthetic, simulated, derived, calibrated -- and what it may be derived from
observation_schema.does_not_mean: that a synthetic or simulated value is a measurement

run_identity.authority: scientific/run_identity.py :: run_identity_for -- model, implementation digest, validated parameters, environment, backend status; scientific/backend_probe.py :: runtime_record -- the backend the worker actually runs on
run_identity.means: what counts as 'the same run' for reuse: a RESOLVED backend, identical in every recorded part (D-2026-94)
run_identity.does_not_mean: cross-machine equivalence: a run on another numeric backend -- SIMD set, core, thread or dispatch settings, native build, installed bytes, the kernel a BLAS selected, the system libraries -- is a different run (D-2026-90, D-2026-94), and no policy yet says when two backends agree well enough for a given model; nor that an UNRESOLVED backend is the same as anything, itself included -- it is recomputed

claims_boundary.authority: CLAIMS_BOUNDARY.md (prose) + docs/claims_boundary.json + tools/claims_enforcement.py :: the generic epistemic boundaries, each held to the code and tests that enforce it
claims_boundary.means: which kinds of result may never be presented as which others
claims_boundary.does_not_mean: a list of sentences: each boundary is enforced by a schema or a gate, named

release_trust_policy.authority: docs/supply_chain_ci_policy.json + tools/supply_chain.py :: what a CI-validation signature attests and how it is verified; no release trust root exists
release_trust_policy.means: who built which bytes in CI, and that they are the bytes signed
release_trust_policy.does_not_mean: that the content is scientifically correct, or that a release is authorized: a signature is provenance, and a release needs the owner's authorization

provenance_records.authority: final_manifest.json (every git-tracked file except the two detached ones, per-file SHA-256) + manifest_hash.txt (detached SHA-256 of the manifest); generator generate_manifest.py (reads the git index). The file count is not restated here: it is whatever the git index holds, and generate_manifest.py --check is the authority on membership.
provenance_records.means: these bytes were present at this SHA-256
provenance_records.does_not_mean: that the file is a governed scientific authority; semantic authority is registered in this file and in AUTHORITIES.md, never conferred by manifest membership

scientific_stack_adoption.authority: STACK.md (narrative) + stack.json (machine-readable, schema 2.0.0, validated by tools/stack_registry.py) :: adoption ladder for every stack element; code is the authority and both mirror it
scientific_stack_adoption.implementation: scientific/integrations/ (VTK, OpenUSD, OpenMDAO), scientific/sensitivity.py (SALib cross-check), agent_substrate/rag_index.py (read-only retrieval), scientific/checks/fenicsx_slab.py and scientific/fmi_boundary.py (FEniCSx and FMI, out of process)
consumers: tests/test_stack_registry.py (the registry validated and held to the code)
scientific_stack_adoption.note: additive and workspace-only: no scientific model imports an integration, every writer refuses to write outside verification/, authority_effect=NONE, and the tree_untouched rule re-verifies final_manifest.json after the workflow runs

agent_authority_substrate.authority: agent_substrate/authority.py :: the transition table and invariants I1-I6 that decide what may become canonical; agent_substrate/events.py :: the append-only hash-chained log that is the only writable record of those decisions, serialized across processes by an advisory lock; agent_substrate/evidence.py :: the content-addressed store that makes a cited digest resolvable, which is what turns I6 from a shape check into an existence check; agent_substrate/capability.py :: CapabilityLedger, the grants IN FORCE projected from the log rather than assembled by the caller, so a grant the log never recorded authorizes nothing; agent_substrate/checkpoint.py :: a cached verification result, never a second source of truth -- every use is reported as weaker than a full verification; agent_substrate/safeio.py :: confined reads -- the authorized root opened once as a descriptor, every component opened descriptor-relative with O_NOFOLLOW, the OPENED object validated rather than the pathname, and a cited digest binding the result to content; agent_substrate/readpath.py :: who may read what, default-deny and recorded; agent_substrate/canonical.py :: the one byte representation every digest in the layer is taken over
agent_authority_substrate.implementation: agent_substrate/ -- canonical (serialization), events (log, separate head witness, anchored incremental verification), evidence (content-addressed, self-verifying, append-only), capability (authority as a bounded object), tools (default-deny registry), execution (kernel-bounded subprocesses), checkpoint (cached verification results and projection snapshots), authority (state machine), policy (versioned rule documents, deny-overrides, decisions that name the document digest that decided), secrets (references that travel and values that do not), netauth (egress as a bounded grant, default deny), store (live projection, optimistic concurrency, idempotency keys that record what they completed), invalidation (transitive staleness derived from the transition table), reconstruct (a deliberately separate replay compared against the live projection), tasks (durable work lifecycle), scheduler (the durable queue: readiness, leases, classified retry, cancellation cascade), memory (remembered statements, structurally unable to become evidence), context (what the agent was shown, recorded apart from what is true), audit (turning the log into answers), governed_tasks (the production caller)
consumers: tests/test_agent_substrate.py (transition table, log integrity, projection, invalidation, reconstruction)
tests/test_agent_substrate_properties.py (Hypothesis property and stateful testing; invariants asserted on every reachable state)
tests/test_agent_substrate_isolation.py (authority_effect=NONE and the declared layering, enforced rather than described)
tests/test_agent_evidence.py (the store, and the gate wired to it)
tests/test_agent_checkpoint.py (checkpoints, anchors, snapshots, and the limits of each)
tests/test_agent_execution.py (capabilities, tool contracts, bounded execution, and the ledger that makes a grant real)
tests/test_agent_policy.py, test_agent_scheduler.py, test_agent_netauth.py, test_agent_secrets.py, test_agent_memory.py, test_agent_context.py, test_agent_agents.py (one per subsystem)
tests/test_agent_audit.py (task chains, authority-record chains, policy decisions, and the provenance holes each can hide)
tests/test_agent_crash_recovery.py, test_agent_concurrency.py, test_agent_long_horizon.py (what survives a kill, a race, and a restart)
tests/test_agent_performance.py, test_agent_fuzz.py (asymptotic guards and a committed fuzz regression corpus)

tests/test_agent_hostile_campaign.py (ONE hostile agent, sixteen escalating attempts against one shared log, then what the whole history shows; it found the replay re-authorizing against a starting state the writer supplied)

tests/test_agent_readpath.py (the read boundary attacked at the open: traversal, symlinks at every position, FIFOs, sockets, devices, hard-link aliases, driven races between authorization and open, and capability scope)
tests/test_agent_governed_tasks.py (THE PRODUCTION CALLER, end to end)
Snakefile :: rule governed_tasks (the governed run is part of the build; a provenance gap, an unjoinable policy decision or a gapped authority record fails it)
agent_authority_substrate.does_not_mean: This layer governs how claims ABOUT the project become canonical. It does not govern, compute, or influence any physics. Agent execution cannot directly mutate authoritative scientific state, evidence, or acceptance state except through the governed interfaces and event-derived authority machinery. No solver or scientific model imports agent_substrate/, and nothing here moves an acceptance decision by itself. A record reaching PROMOTED here means a claim was proposed, independently verified, and promoted under a recorded policy -- it does not mean that anything was measured or experimentally validated. Likewise a task reaching VERIFIED on the governed path means a declared tool ran under kernel-enforced CPU, address-space, output-size, process-count and core-dump bounds; was granted no network authority by this substrate; produced the bytes it claims; and a SEPARATED registered actor confirmed those bytes are still on disk. Those are two separate statements and only the first is the kernel's: none of the rlimits restricts networking, a child process can open sockets, and what is withheld is authority rather than capability. The in-process socket guard is a monkeypatch in the parent interpreter and is not containment; it does not exist in a child at all. That is provenance. It is not scientific validity.
agent_authority_substrate.note: Enforcement is verified by mutation testing rather than by coverage: each check is deleted in turn and the suite must fail. tools/mutation_matrix.py exits non-zero on a survivor, on an anchor that no longer matches its source, on a source not restored byte-identically, on collateral damage to a tracked file, or on a post-run baseline that no longer passes; it refuses to start against a red baseline OR a non-deterministic one. The harness is itself mutated by tools/mutations/mutation_harness.json, after a defect was found in it: it could run a mutation against the PREVIOUS mutation's cached bytecode whenever both changed the file by the same number of bytes within one mtime second, which reported kills for mutations nothing had tested. A second harness defect was found the same way: its collateral-damage restore is 'git checkout HEAD --', which cannot tell a suite-damaged file from an uncommitted edit, and it destroyed real work twice in one session; the restore still happens and the discarded bytes are now kept under .mutation-quarantine/. A surviving mutation means a check is unprotected, not that it is redundant. Mutation testing asks whether a check that EXISTS is load-bearing; it cannot ask whether one is MISSING, because there is nothing to delete. Two techniques cover that: Hypothesis state machines over the authority, task and job machines, and a hostile-agent campaign against the governed path. Each found defects the other could not -- the campaign found the task replay re-authorizing a forged record against the starting state the record itself declared, which let one appended line move a task out of the sealed VERIFIED state. Narrative form: AGENT_SUBSTRATE.md; per-requirement status: docs/completion_matrix.json.
agent_authority_substrate.status: BUILT_AND_VERIFIED_WITH_PRODUCTION_CALLERS: agent_substrate/governed_tasks.py and agent_substrate/governed_model.py are invoked by the Snakefile's governed_tasks, governed_index and governed_model rules, so the substrate has consumers that do real work and write files somebody reads. tests/test_agent_substrate_isolation.py enforces the narrow, named crossing that permits it (three bridge modules reaching one thing, the workspace guard in scientific/workspace.py) and still forbids the other direction absolutely. A scientific result reaches VERIFIED only through a governed run, an independent check and a distinct reviewer; PROMOTED remains a state reached only in tests, and promoting a result is a separate change that must name which results it governs and who holds each role.

repository_content.authority: tools/repo_content_audit.py + docs/repo_content_audit.json :: what the current tree may carry; tools/repo_inventory.py + docs/repository_inventory.json :: what happened to every file of the baseline commit
repository_content.means: that no tracked file carries the retired hardware programme -- its paths, imports, gate dependencies or vocabulary -- and that every baseline file is classified with its disposition applied
repository_content.does_not_mean: that git history no longer contains it: ordinary deletion removes files from the tree, never from history
